title: Set 74

sentences.ko: 싱크대 고치는 법 좀 찾아보려고 앉았는데, 영상은 2분 만에 찾았거든. 근데 어쩌다 보니 밤 열두 시고 나는 웬 아저씨가 낡은 타자기 고치는 걸 보고 있는 거야. 정작 필요한 건 적어 놓지도 않았어. 그래서 싱크대는 아직도 물이 새고, 오늘 밤에 그걸 처음부터 다시 해야 돼.
sentences.text: I sat down to look up how to fix the sink, and I found the video in about two minutes, and then somehow it's midnight and I'm watching a guy restore an old typewriter. I never even wrote down what I actually needed. So the sink is still dripping and I get to do the whole thing over tonight.

alts.text: So I'm looking up how to fix the sink, right, and I find the video in like two minutes, and then somehow it's midnight and I'm watching some guy restore an old typewriter. Never even wrote down what I actually needed. Sink's still dripping, so I get to do the whole thing over again tonight.

I sat down to research how to repair the sink, and I located the video in approximately two minutes, and then it was somehow midnight and I was watching a man restore an old typewriter. I never even wrote down what I actually needed. The sink is still dripping, so I must do the entire thing over again tonight.

sentences.note: **look up** 은 사전이나 인터넷에서 무언가를 찾아본다는 뜻입니다. **do the whole thing over** 는 했던 일을 처음부터 다시 한다는 말입니다.
sentences.situation: 유튜브 보다가 시간 다 날린 얘기

sentences.ko: 우리 예전에 목요일 일정을 통째로 그 드라마에 맞춰서 짰던 거 기억나? 새 시즌 한 십오 분쯤 봤는데 벌써 폰만 보고 있더라. 게다가 대본 쓰는 사람들은 그대로거든. 그래서 자꾸 내가 변한 건가 싶어. 근데 내 문제는 아닌 것 같아.
sentences.text: You remember how we used to plan our whole Thursday around that show? I got about fifteen minutes into the new season and I was already on my phone. And it's the same people writing it, so I keep thinking maybe it's me. I don't think it's me.

alts.text: Remember when our whole Thursday was built around that show? Fifteen minutes into the new season and I'm already on my phone. And it's the same people writing it, so I keep thinking maybe it's me. I don't think it's me though.

Do you remember how we used to arrange our entire Thursday around that show? I was about fifteen minutes into the new season and I was already looking at my phone. It is written by the same people, so I keep wondering whether it is me. I do not believe it is me.

sentences.note: **plan our whole Thursday around that show** 처럼 plan A around B 는 B 를 중심에 두고 A 를 짠다는 뜻입니다. **maybe it's me** 는 문제가 상대가 아니라 내 쪽에 있나 싶을 때 씁니다.

sentences.ko: 이건 너만 알고 있어. 나 사실 차 막혀서 늦은 거 아니야. 첫 번째 알람은 자느라 못 들었고, 두 번째는 잠도 안 깬 채로 그냥 미뤄 버렸어. 별일도 아닌데 너무 늦게까지 안 자서 그래. 회사에는 길이 막혔다고 했어. 솔직히 진짜 막혔을 수도 있지, 나야 모르지. 아무도 더 캐묻지 않더라.
sentences.text: Don't say anything, but I wasn't stuck in traffic. I slept through the first alarm and then I hit snooze on the second one without even waking up, because I was up way too late for no reason. I told them the roads were backed up, and honestly they might have been, I wouldn't know. Nobody asked me a single follow up question.

alts.text: Keep this to yourself, but the traffic thing wasn't true. I slept right through the first alarm and then snoozed the second one without even waking up, 'cause I was up way too late for no reason. Told them the roads were backed up, and honestly they might've been, no idea. Not one follow up question.

Please do not repeat this, but I was not stuck in traffic. I slept through the first alarm and then pressed snooze on the second one without even waking up, because I had stayed up far too late for no reason. I told them the roads were congested, and in fairness they may well have been, I would not know. Nobody asked me a single follow up question.

sentences.note: **hit snooze** 는 알람의 다시 울림 버튼을 누른다는 말입니다. **follow up question** 은 들은 말에 이어서 더 파고드는 질문입니다.

sentences.ko: 우리 개가 고른 건 우리 형이야. 형은 한 달에 두 번쯤 오는데. 밥 주는 것도 나고, 비 쏟아지는 새벽 여섯 시에 데리고 나가는 것도 난데, 형이 문 열고 들어오는 순간 나는 없는 사람이 돼. 서운하다는 건 아니야. 그래, 조금은 서운해.
sentences.text: Our dog picked my brother, and my brother comes over maybe twice a month. I feed him, I take him out at six in the morning when it's pouring, and then my brother walks in the door and I don't exist. I'm not bitter about it. Okay, I'm a little bitter about it.

alts.text: My brother's the one our dog picked, and he's over maybe twice a month. I'm the one feeding him, taking him out at six in the morning when it's pouring, and then my brother walks in and I don't exist. I'm not bitter. Okay, I'm a little bitter.

Our dog chose my brother, and my brother visits perhaps twice a month. I feed him, I take him out at six in the morning when it is pouring, and then my brother comes through the door and I do not exist. I am not bitter about it. Admittedly, I am a little bitter about it.

sentences.note: **I'm not bitter about it** 은 서운하지 않다고 말하면서 사실은 서운함을 드러낼 때 자주 씁니다. 뒤에 Okay 로 바로 뒤집는 것까지가 한 세트입니다.

sentences.ko: 봄에 빵 만들기에 완전 빠져 있었거든. 발효종을 주방 조리대에 올려놓고 하루도 안 빼놓고 먹였어. 그러다 주말에 어디 좀 다녀왔는데 그새 죽어 버렸고, 그 뒤로 다시 시작을 안 했어. 밀가루는 아직 찬장에 그대로 있어. 끝났다고 인정하기가 아직 싫은가 봐.
sentences.text: I got really into making bread in the spring, like I had the starter sitting on the counter and I was feeding it every single day. Then we went away for a weekend and it died, and I never started another one. The flour's still in the cupboard, so I guess I'm not ready to admit it's over.

alts.text: Bread was my whole thing in the spring, like the starter's sitting on the counter and I'm feeding it every single day. Then we went away for a weekend and it died, and I never started another one. Flour's still in the cupboard, so I guess I'm not ready to say it's over.

I became quite absorbed in making bread in the spring. I kept the starter on the counter and I fed it every single day. Then we went away for a weekend and it died, and I never began another one. The flour is still in the cupboard, so I suppose I am not ready to admit that it is over.

sentences.note: **got really into** 는 한동안 무언가에 푹 빠졌다는 뜻입니다. **it's over** 는 그 일이 이제 끝났다는 말입니다.

reviewed: 3번: 앞에서는 "차가 막혀서 늦은 게 아니다"라고 해 놓고 뒤에서는 회사에 "지하철이 엉망이었다"고 했다고 해서, 둘러댄 핑계가 두 개가 되어 헷갈렸습니다. 뒤쪽을 길 막힘(the roads were backed up)으로 맞춰 하나로 정리했습니다.
3번 한국어의 "내가 알 게 뭐야"는 "관심 없다"는 뜻이라 영어의 I wouldn't know(나는 알 수가 없다)와 뜻이 다릅니다. "나야 모르지"로 고쳤습니다.
3번 casual 의 Nobody asked me one follow up question 은 원어민이 그렇게 말하지 않습니다. Not one follow up question. 으로 바꿨습니다.
4번 formal 의 Very well 은 부탁을 받아들일 때 쓰는 말이라, 여기 Okay(마지못해 인정하는 자리)와 맞지 않습니다. Admittedly 로 바꿨습니다.
2번 한국어의 "내 탓은 아닌 것 같아"는 책임 소재 얘기로 들립니다. 원문은 "문제가 내 쪽에 있나" 싶다는 말이라 "내 문제는 아닌 것 같아"로 고쳤습니다.
